name: Kyrgyzstan

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 90%, Orthodox Christian about 7%

snapshot: Sadyr Japarov broke with his powerful security chief in 2026, and a court later convicted the former ally of plotting to seize power.
culture: Kyrgyz identity rests on nomadic traditions and the Manas epic, one of the longest poems in the world, recited from memory by manaschi bards. The World Nomad Games, featuring horseback sports like kok-boru, a kind of polo with a goat carcass, have been hosted in Kyrgyzstan. Yurts still dot the summer pastures.
society: Remittances from Kyrgyz workers in Russia are a large share of GDP. Trade with Russia has boomed, some of it re-exports of goods under Western sanctions. Kyrgyzstan was once Central Asia's most open political system, with three presidents toppled by protests, but has turned authoritarian since 2020.
baseline: Sadyr Japarov rose to power after 2020 protests, then expanded presidential powers through a 2021 constitution. In February 2026 he dismissed Kamchybek Tashiev, the security chief seen as his partner and potential successor, after an open letter called for early elections; in July a court convicted Tashiev of attempting to seize power and gave him a suspended sentence. A presidential election is due in early 2027.

leaders.gov: Chairman of the Cabinet Adylbek Kasymaliev
